photos.c:
The caption that goes with this photograph in our archives reads:
"Walk Match at Battersea circa 1938. Starters include H.G. Churcher, C.E.Churcher, D.E. Brown, A.A.Harley, F. Jarvis, C.W.Redgrave."
Our first stab at actually naming the faces came up with Don Brown (1), Harry Churcher (7), Charlie Churcher (23), C.W. Redgrave (24) and Alf Harley (behind Brown). However, as others have become involved and have cast their eyes over the picture, we are now not at all sure of anyone except Alf Harley. For instance, we are told that Charlie Churcher did not wear glasses and the chap next to Harry, second from the left, may be Jack Rutland If any reader can help us with more specific details of the race then we would be very pleased to hear from them.

photos.c: Front Cover. Injured for much of the season John Regis has managed to peak for the big ones and has produced an incredible list of performances including; Winning the Junior AAA's indoor 200m in a CBP, winning the U.K. Senior 200m, gaining an individual bronze in the European Junior 100m, a team gold in the short relay at the same Championship and culminating with a new Club record for the 200m of 20.78.
An "unfit" John Regis was persuaded to run a 400m relay leg in the first B.A.L. Match at Birmingham and clocked an impressive 45.36 split - wearing his new "1 piece".
Front page: Regis to Ridgeon - the Belgrave baton passes from one 1987 World Championship medallist to another.

The 4x400 metres final. Roger Black and Derek Redmond have done their work well and now it is up to John Regis to keep breathing down the neck of the USA's Danny Everett. The Belgravian does a fine job, leaving Kris Akabusi to wait ... and wait ... and then strike for gold in the last two metres.
John Regis (1) takes the back stretch, passing the baton on to Simon Shirley (2) at New River Stadium during B.A.L. match 4.

Back page: John Regis races to 1st place in the Pearl Assurance UK Championships 200 metres final at Crystal Palace. What a season this man has had, setting bests of 10.15, 19.94 and 45.48, and taking the IAAF World Championships silver medal behind Frankie Fredericks of Namibia. Photo by Gray Mortimore, Allsport.
Left: the fastest Belgrave sprint relay squad of all time - left to right - Neil Owen, John Regis, Lenny Paul, Phil Goedluck - 40.05!

BELS IN BUDAPEST

Top (left to right): Phil Spivey watches Racing Club's Yuri Sedykh put the competition beyond anyone else's reach while preparing for his own throw. While eventual 'chase winner Lambruschini lopes along at the back, Justin Chaston is in the thick of the action. Discus thrower Darrin Morris placed 5th. A "home team" decision may have cost shot-putter Paul Edwards 2nd place.
Bottom: Neil Owen surges through the high hurdles field after his blocks slipped. Derek Browne had five no jumps before a superb last effort overtook a class field including one time Olympic Champion Khristo Markhov. John Regis relaxes in the shade before a scintillating 10.15 100m - as a non-scorer! Spearman Niigel Bevan fires a 3rd-placing 71.78.
Photos by Alan Mead. Colour-spread sponsored by Tom Carter.
The Master and The Apprentice: John Regis takes the baton from 17 year-old Chris Lambert.

photos.c: The start of the Belgrave 800 metre championship for 1991. From left to right: Nigel Clarke, Jon Coy, Mark Anderson, Brandon Reid, Gavin Teahan, Colin Bond and Tony Stone.
Into the second lap of the Senior Men's 1500 metres with, left to right, Gavin Teahan, Marcello Bizio, Brandon Reid, Adam Armstrong (hidden), Nigel Clarke and Trevor Williams still in contention.

Opposite page: The "last" Belgrave-Southern Relay.
Top. High noon and the starter sends 61 runners off on the first leg. Jon Hobbs completes his lap of the "top" and nears the crowd at the Hand in Hand.
Centre. Ollie Foote sends Marcello Bizio away on the last stage. Jim Estall loosens up for the London Marathon with a 25:53 long leg. Second fastest long stage of the day and another mark in the all-time top 20 - Paul Evans has an easy run!
Bottom. Jim Estall launches Marco Mazzotta. Frank Ward reaches the summit of Wool Road. Putting on a good show for visiting relations, "Aussie" Brandon Reid streaks off the Common for a nippy second leg.

Australian Brandon Reid has contributed greatly to Belgrave teams over the past few seasons. Road relays ... Southern League 800s ... British League 1500s ... he has given his best in all of them. Now it's time to say goodbye as he heads back home. Best wishes Brandon. Let us know how your running progresses and let's hope you can make it back to Wimbledon some time.

photos.c: Above: The start of the Eastleigh 10k on March 19th.  The race included the CAU Inter-Counties Championship and Belgravians were racing in some unfamiliar vests.  In the red vest with white/red shorts towards the left is the eventual race winner Angus Maclean (Team Southampton). 31 is Richard Ward (Belgrave/Surrey), 32 Phil Wicks (Belgrave/Surrey), between and just behind  these latter two is Tim Watson in a white/green vest (Belgrave/Hampshire).  To the right of Phil is Hassan Raidi (Belgrave/Surrey), Jonathan Blackledge (Belgrave), and 15 Jermain Mays (Kent AC/Kent).  Maclean's winning time was 29:47, Mays was second in 30:00 and Phil Wicks 3rd in 30:02.  Belgrave won the team race and Surrey the Inter-County Championship. Full result and report in the previous issue.  Photo by Steve Wicks.

To the right of Phil is Hassan Raidi (Belgrave/Surrey), Jonathan Blackledge (Belgrave), and 15 Jermain Mays (Kent AC/Kent). photos.c:
The caption that goes with this photograph in our archives reads:
"Walk Match at Battersea circa 1938. Starters include H.G. Churcher, C.E.Churcher, D.E. Brown, A.A.Harley, F. Jarvis, C.W.Redgrave."
Our first stab at actually naming the faces came up with Don Brown (1), Harry Churcher (7), Charlie Churcher (23), C.W. Redgrave (24) and Alf Harley (behind Brown). However, as others have become involved and have cast their eyes over the picture, we are now not at all sure of anyone except Alf Harley. For instance, we are told that Charlie Churcher did not wear glasses and the chap next to Harry, second from the left, may be Jack Rutland If any reader can help us with more specific details of the race then we would be very pleased to hear from them.

photos.c: Above: The start of the inaugural AAA 5 km Road Championship, held in conjunction with the Horwich Carnival race.  From left to right Peter Riley (107 Leigh H), Rob Whalley (90 Bristol & West AC), Andi Jones (51 Salford), David Anderson (88 Belgrave H) with Mark Miles on his left, behind Ian Mitchell (114 Tipton), the eventual winner Wilf Taragon (85 Birchfield), Mark Tucker (126 Australia), Birhan Dagne (217 Belgrave H) is on the right.  Mark Miles placed second with the fastest time run by a Briton in Britain this year – 13:58 – and took the AAA Championship.

Above: The AAA 5k Road Race was again held in Horwich. It was only the second time the Championship has been held and the Bels have medalled on each occasion – silver in 2005 and now gold in 2006. Individual AAA Champion was Chris Davies of Telford (in the red and yellow), second was Peter Riley of Leigh (white vest with green diagonal) and third was our own Mark Miles (177). Simon Jones (not pictured) and Richard Ward (181) made up the Belgrave team. The Open race was won by Birchfield, running three Africans, but they were not eligible for the AAA race.
